scope: Theorem 3.1 (Local phase assertion) of the manuscript “Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs” (preprints/Minimal-models-and-Mori-fibre-spaces-for-generalized-log-canonical-Q-pairs-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 036 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 37e6d650c989c3fb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Vi, oi) be a sequence of pointed algebraic Gorenstein klt germs of a fixed dimension n ≥ 2, with oi closed. Suppose that a finite cyclic group Gi acts on an affine representative of each germ, fixes oi, and admits a semi-invariant canonical generator θi, a volume form with zero divisor near oi. Choose an arbitrary element γi ∈ Gi for each i. After passage to a subsequence, there are divisorial valuations w′ i centred at oi, a constant C > 0, and a positive integer ℓ, independent of i on that subsequence, such that Aθi (w′ i) ≤ C and, for every nonzero rational semi-invariant function h on Vi of character χ, (3.1) w′ i(h) ≡ ℓ angle ( χ(γi) ) (mod Z). In particular, w′ i restricts to an integral-valued valuation of C(Vi)Gi .
